title: Prefix-Ratio GRPO: Improving Gradient Quality for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards

contributions.purpose: Corrects for staleness in distributed RL for LLMs by accounting for sequential dependencies that per-token importance sampling ignores.
contributions.mechanism: Prefix-Ratio GRPO modifies GRPO importance ratios with a prefix-aware ratio rho-tilde_t = (min_{k<t} rho_k) * rho_t, downweighting all tokens that follow any token that has become unlikely under the current policy (a bad prefix).
contributions.evaluation: On AIME24 at staleness S = 11, achieves 0.500 avg@64 versus vanilla GRPO's 0.400 (+10pp).
contributions.domain: distributed RL with verifiable rewards / LLM reasoning
contributions.source_quote: We propose Prefix-Ratio GRPO, a simple modification to GRPO that incorporates prefix information into importance ratios, enabling selective gradient dampening based on prefix quality.

contributions.purpose: Demonstrates performance gains under high staleness against standard baselines.
contributions.mechanism: Benchmark comparison of Prefix-Ratio GRPO against vanilla GRPO and tight-clip GRPO under distributed training staleness.
contributions.evaluation: On AIME24 at staleness S = 11, Prefix-Ratio GRPO achieves 0.500 avg@64, outperforming vanilla GRPO (0.400, +10pp) and tight-clip GRPO (0.367, +13.3pp).
contributions.domain: mathematical reasoning benchmarks / LLM RL training
contributions.source_quote: On AIME24 at staleness S = 11, Prefix-Ratio GRPO achieves 0.500 avg@64, outperforming vanilla GRPO (0.400, +10pp) and tight-clip GRPO (0.367, +13.3pp).

contributions.purpose: Verifies that the dampening mechanism is selective rather than uniformly suppressive.
contributions.mechanism: Selectivity analysis measuring the fraction of bad-prefix versus good-prefix tokens dampened by the prefix-aware ratio.
contributions.evaluation: Achieves a 4.42x selectivity ratio, dampening 99.4% of bad-prefix tokens while only dampening 22.6% of good-prefix tokens.
contributions.source_quote: We provide selectivity analysis showing Prefix-Ratio GRPO achieves 4.42x selectivity ratio, dampening 99.4% of bad-prefix tokens while only dampening 22.6% of good-prefix tokens.

self_declared_provenance.quote: MinPRO (Lei et al., 2026) introduces prefix importance ratios for stabilizing policy optimization under off-policy conditions ... Our work applies similar intuition to gradient quality improvement: we use prefix-aware ratios to selectively dampen gradients from tokens following bad reasoning prefixes, improving downstream performance rather than focusing solely on training stability.
We propose Prefix-Ratio GRPO, a simple modification to GRPO that incorporates prefix information into importance ratios.

notes: Positive-result paper; evaluation appears limited to a single benchmark (AIME24) at a single staleness setting (S=11) in the claimed contributions. Method closely parallels MinPRO's prefix importance ratio per the paper's own related-work positioning. Paper carries an automated-research-system generation warning.
